summary: Penor 02 studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang. He also taught Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé.

Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Penor Rinpoche studied at Palyul Monastery and under teachers including Thubten Chökyi Dawa, Karma Tekchok Nyingpo, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Jampel Gyepai Dorje. He founded the Ngagyur Nyingma Institute in 1978.

Pentti Aalto worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1934–1940) under Gustaf John Ramstedt (~1935–1950) and served there as Docent of Comparative Linguistics from 1958 to 1980.

Per Kjeld Sørensen specializes in Tibetology and Indology. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Erik Haarh, later lecturing there (1982–1989). He served as a professor at the University of Leipzig (1994–2017) and held visiting roles at Bonn and UC Berkeley.

Per Kvaerne, a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies, completed his Ph.D. at the University of Oslo by 1973. He served as a professor at the University of Oslo (attested 1978, 1991–1996) and as Secretary General of the International Association for Tibetan Studies.

Per Kværne worked in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Mag. art. and Dr. phil. at the University of Oslo, lectured at the University of Bergen (1970–1975), and was a professor at the University of Oslo (1975–2007).

Peri Bhaskararao worked in linguistics and Indology. He served as Professor of Phonetics and Phonology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1977–1996) and held a post at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1996–2012).
Peri Sarveswara Sharma worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Wilhelm Rau (~1965–1970) and held a post at the University of Marburg from around 1970 to 1991.

Sinologist Perry Link earned his B.A. from Harvard University (~1962–1966). He taught Chinese language and literature at UCLA (1977–1988), held a post at Princeton (1973–1977), and held a Chancellorial Chair at UC Riverside (~2008).

Perry Schmidt-Leukel works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed his degrees and Habilitation at the University of Munich (~1977–1996), later serving as professor at the University of Glasgow (2000–2009) and the University of Münster (2009–2023).

Peter Adamson specializes in philosophy and Indology. He studied at Williams College (~1990–1994) and the University of Notre Dame (~1994–2000). He held posts at King's College London (~2000–2012) and the University of Munich (~2012).

Peter Alan Roberts works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied with traditional teacher Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche in 1979 and completed doctoral research supervised by Michael Aris and Richard Gombrich.

Peter C. Bisschop specializes in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Groningen under Hans T. Bakker and Harunaga Isaacson, later holding posts at Wolfson College, Oxford, the University of Edinburgh (2005–2010), and Leiden University.
Peter Connolly works in religious studies and Indology. He completed his BA, MA, and Ph.D. at Lancaster University and became a Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Chichester in 1980.

Peter D. Hershock works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Yale University and under traditional teachers Seungsahn Haengwon and Ji Kwang Dae Poep Sa Nim. He directed the East-West Center's Asian Studies Development Program and held an appointment at the University of Hawaiʱi.
Peter Dronke worked in history and archaeology. He studied at Magdalen College (~1955–1958) and held a post at the University of Cambridge from around 1961 to 2001.
Peter Ebbatson is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Oxford under the supervision of Walpola Rahula.
Peter Fenner works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Noble Ross Reat, Arvind Sharma, and Richard A. Hutch, and held a post at Deakin University.

Peter Francis Kornicki works in Japanology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Oxford and Tokyo University of Education, he studied under Masamichi Asukai and Mitsukuni Yoshida, teaching at the University of Tasmania, Kyoto University, and Robinson College and the University of Cambridge.

Peter Gaeffke worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied in Regensburg, Mainz (PhD under Ernst Schwarz), and Dublin. He held posts at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, Utrecht University (Professor 1964), and the University of Pennsylvania (Professor 1975–2003).
